label: Romanisation · the title
rom: Sulter sa vorr
english: IV.5 · The Burning Boat

label: Romanisation · the dateline
rom: Ul et syst pawast, ul Hyll Pawast.
english: *The second summer, in the Second Tide.*

label: Romanisation · Seren’s headnote
rom: Re hadh Voss sa re vess, hosen re wrodh scaelur Voss, Elspet, o lo, lo ey vorr um dhavow Dhavow Hemm. El trenn o sa nath gadhant et higileth, eth vell sa nath hessent et tevath vellyl; re dhyvull et Orrow umo, eth nath re dhyvull et wadh.
english: *Laid by Voss who asked, as his grandmother Elspet told it him at her fire on the quay at Eldhythe. It is a tale the ship-masters would not tell, and a rhyme the children would not stop singing; the shore laughed at it, and the sea laughed not.*

label: Romanisation
rom: Hebb et tolm lom. Nel en drenn sy. El trenn en scaelur; eth re yal o loy hy ey vost, eth re yal o lo hy et wadh.
english: Give me the stone. This one is not mine. It is my grandmother's, and she had it from her brother, and he had it from the sea.

label: Romanisation
rom: Ul gethyl hosast et gorrol sy, um et dhysal, re hunnom scethel ul vorrol. Re scyndal o. Lo dhrenn et hald re hylent et farrardath hemm lerneth hy et wadh, eth Merrik hosast. Um et hald rerddhalden re hossvell Yory.
english: In the first holding of this war, on the shingle, I heard one of their hulls burn. It screamed. Along the wall the old sailors turned their faces from the sea, and Merrick first. On the east wall Jory whistled.

label: Romanisation
rom: Re hyl tevvell ulom hosen bunth hunneryl. Amm re yal dhom surr lom, re hunnerym lo. Amm re yal pa vurr surr lom, re hyrrilym o.
english: A rhyme went round in me like a skipping-rope. At seven I had skipped to it. At forty I understood it.

label: Romanisation
rom: Amm ew luld en lo ey genth, re vessym en scaelur hy vodh nath hunnant et higileth o. Re dhess ey lom; ew trenn o. Nydha o, nalelv ell lelv.
english: A boy at her table, I asked my grandmother wherefore the ship-masters would not hear it. She answered me with a tale. Ye may weigh it.

label: Romanisation
rom: Amm re yal delv surr loy, re heth ey et vorr ul davowlest ey odha. Re vellorant et higileth hy et helvnynth, eth et helv ul so vern. Ul susk et vorr re haemer sull tolm ryss myst, eth tolmath umont, bynt hosen miskryteth nasath um rull thenth. Re sesk nahos vodh re vyskent. Nath re vessent veth et tevath. Re runnant et higileth mygurath um et tolm vimm sost.
english: At twelve she kept the fire in her mother's harbour-house. In out of the rain came the ship-masters, with the weather in their beards. Over the fire hung three flat grey stones, with letters fine as the tracks of birds on wet sand. What they said, none wist. Only the children asked. The ship-masters knocked out their pipes on the lowest one.

label: Romanisation
rom: Amm re vymm berderd hy et myst, eth trenn lo, re dhyvull ey, eth re losk ey et nunth. Kyl Mystow uldath venn dem nyculardath, re vysk ey.
english: At every bold man home from the grey with a tale she laughed, and filled his cup. "The Mystlands make liars of honest men," said she.

label: Romanisation
rom: Re vysk ey o um ey vost.
english: She said it of her brother.

label: Romanisation
rom: Ew gostard Daveth ul et gostol. Ul et syst ull re yal o ul mymmyl dem varn hy lern et myst, ul hos hy et sultereth dasken et mesk domm, vimm ul et wadh; eth sulter pawast ul o sestow.
english: Daveth was an axeman of the felling. That summer he was coming home from the edge in one of the last timber-boats, low with black wood, and a second in his wake.

label: Romanisation
rom: Re rarr sulter umonta hy et myst, ul vorr, ul lern et helvhoss eth ul lern et kess; nath noss darrol hosen sy lo sulter. Ul scyndalol re rarr o, hosen darrant wadhnasath um luldath sa rikent hy nasow. Vimm re runn o umonta, ul vodh re haemer et havul nalelv sost, eth re rik et mesk domm sa re lymme et vorr hyo. Ul sestow re rarr et helvnynth, um wisketh pa hryrull.
english: Out of the grey a boat came at them, burning, into the wind and against the current, which no boat can do. Screaming it came, as gulls come at boys that rob a nest. Low it struck them both, where the load rode heaviest, and the black wood in their holds took its fire. After came the rain, on the heads of two crews.

label: Romanisation
rom: Re vymment sull dem varn.
english: Three came home.

label: Romanisation
rom: Re vymm Daveth dem varn um vivenn cresket, eth et wadh ul vidhyl hy o hovv um et pressir sa re vidh en scaelur. Hosen ull re wrodh ey o lom. Ul et bremm ull tunn re wrodhant et sull o, eth nafedh pawast re hadhant misk ul sulter.
english: Daveth came home on a spar, with the sea running out of his coat onto the floor my grandmother had swept. So she told it me. All that autumn the three told it, and never again set foot in a boat.

label: Romanisation
rom: Hy ull re rytent uldath et deldvar lo so nunthath um sulter hastat ul vorr, eth uld sennet ulo. Ul neld, re rytent, re hyl o. Um et scyndal re rytent mest hy gor yalat, eth um sull brod orrowen sa re vysk et uld myst; veth um vodh sull, nath re hemme fedh pa hyont.
english: After them the outpost men sware in their cups to a boat shoved off burning, with a dead man in it. Well out, they sware, it turned. To the scream they sware above all, and to three words of ours the grey man spake; but which three, no two agreed.

label: Romanisation
rom: Re nydh ey et sultereth lom um ey nindeth, hosen re nydh Daveth so loy. Hos nind, eth ullen. Hy ull re hadh ey garl ryss um et genth.
english: She counted the boats for me on her fingers, as her brother had counted them for her. One finger, and another. Then she laid her hand flat on the board.

label: Romanisation
rom: Re yal pa sulter.
english: There were two boats.

label: Romanisation
rom: Amm sy myskent et higileth: murr.
english: Now the ship-masters say twenty.

label: Romanisation
rom: Re dhyvull et Orrow um et sull hy et mivenn. Ul morl re dhyvull ey lo, eth re losk ey et nunthath ul vimm et tolm vimm sost.
english: The shore laughed at the three from the spar. By day she laughed with it, and filled their cups under the lowest stone.

label: Romanisation
rom: Ul vess nath re dhyvull ey.
english: At night she did not laugh.

label: Romanisation
rom: Re fimm Daveth um o dhrenn, eth re felm et tavow o, hos drigyl dholm hy lest o odha.
english: Daveth drank on his tale, and the harbour drowned him a stone's throw from his mother's house.

label: Romanisation
rom: Hy vodh nath hunnant et higileth o? Re veskym higil sa re hadh et nunth, eth re orr ul helvnynth, hy vodh nath re vaver o hunnol et trenn. Hy ull re hunnom sull hyont, ul et hiskenneth, gor wrod cadhat hosen nunth.
english: Wherefore would the ship-masters not hear it? I have seen one leave his cup and go out into the rain sooner than hear it. Three of them have I heard since, in the passes, each saying set down like a cup.

label: Romanisation
rom: Sulter lyss ul vorr, ul neld ul et myst, re vysk et hosast. Et pawast: Re hyl o ul lern et helvhoss, eth ul sestow, helv. Et sullast: El et sulter o sa rarr demos amm sennys. Eth et hosast, pawast: Luska et Orrow ul dhyvullol, hy vodh nafedh es narr o dem et Orrow.
english: "A small boat burning, far out in the grey," said the first. The second: "It turned into the wind, and after it, weather." The third: "It is the boat that cometh for you when ye die." And the first again: "Let the shore laugh, for the shore will never have to meet it."

label: Romanisation
rom: Re yal o rytet lo et hinnarath: Besk hespet, hurrat. Sulter vorrat, luskat. Eth cedh brodyorr ul lern ryt?
english: The cities had it in writing: a stranger come armed, and put down, and his boat burned and set adrift. And who will argue with writing?

label: Romanisation
rom: Veth re yal tevvell umo lo et tevath, eth brodyorrant tevath ul lern gor yalat. Re hunnerer lo um et tavow, pa dhev ul gylyl eth hos ul hunneryl. Re hylen et bunth, Yory eth en, hy vodh ew et strom sost eth et niss sost olna; eth lo et lyss sost hyont re hyl Yory o mest niss.
english: But the children had a rhyme for it, and children argue with anything. We skipped to it on the quay, two turning and one jumping. Jory and I turned the rope, for we were the biggest and the slowest, and for the least of them Jory turned it slower yet.

label: Romanisation · the frame
rom: Hy ull re vellent et tevath, hosen vellent o tul:
english: *Then the children sang, as they sing it still:*

label: Romanisation · the verse
rom: Sulter myst, sulter myst, hy et myst,
english:
*Grey boat, grey boat, out of the grey,*
*knelt at the warden's door one day;*
*a stone for a present, a cut for a kiss,*
*and who ever heard of a greeting like this?*
*Burn it and shove it and give it the tide;*
*but the grey boat turned, and the grey boat cried.*

label: Romanisation · the verse
rom: re lumm lo yebb et pard hos ryst;
english:
*Grey boat, grey boat, out of the grey,*
*knelt at the warden's door one day;*
*a stone for a present, a cut for a kiss,*
*and who ever heard of a greeting like this?*
*Burn it and shove it and give it the tide;*
*but the grey boat turned, and the grey boat cried.*

label: Romanisation · the verse
rom: stinel hosen inth, tolm hosen hebbet,
english:
*Grey boat, grey boat, out of the grey,*
*knelt at the warden's door one day;*
*a stone for a present, a cut for a kiss,*
*and who ever heard of a greeting like this?*
*Burn it and shove it and give it the tide;*
*but the grey boat turned, and the grey boat cried.*

label: Romanisation · the verse
rom: eth cemmyl hosen sy, nahunnat!
english:
*Grey boat, grey boat, out of the grey,*
*knelt at the warden's door one day;*
*a stone for a present, a cut for a kiss,*
*and who ever heard of a greeting like this?*
*Burn it and shove it and give it the tide;*
*but the grey boat turned, and the grey boat cried.*

label: Romanisation · the verse
rom: Vorra o, hasta o, hebba o dem hyll;
english:
*Grey boat, grey boat, out of the grey,*
*knelt at the warden's door one day;*
*a stone for a present, a cut for a kiss,*
*and who ever heard of a greeting like this?*
*Burn it and shove it and give it the tide;*
*but the grey boat turned, and the grey boat cried.*

label: Romanisation · the verse
rom: veth re harm sulter myst, eth re hyl.
english:
*Grey boat, grey boat, out of the grey,*
*knelt at the warden's door one day;*
*a stone for a present, a cut for a kiss,*
*and who ever heard of a greeting like this?*
*Burn it and shove it and give it the tide;*
*but the grey boat turned, and the grey boat cried.*

label: Romanisation
rom: Re yal pa dhrenn ullen, sa nath re veller, hy ludal hunnol higil.
english: Two lines more there were, that we sang not, lest a ship-master hear.

label: Romanisation · the verse
rom: Sulter myst ul vorr, eth helvnynth ul sestow;
english:
*Grey boat burning, and after, the rain;*
*and the one it comes for will not come home again.*

label: Romanisation · the verse
rom: eth nath mymm dem varn et hos sa rarr o demo.
english:
*Grey boat burning, and after, the rain;*
*and the one it comes for will not come home again.*

label: Romanisation
rom: Ul hos hedh re hunn Merrik o hyor. Re rik o ol munth, eth re hyl o um o sestyarl, hosen kylent uldath bunth sa haeverent kethyl. Nel ull, re vysk o.
english: One evening Merrick heard us at it. He took our rope, and coiled it on his arm, as men coil a line they mean to keep. "Not that one," said he.

label: Romanisation
rom: Ew Daveth o yedh.
english: His father was Daveth.

label: Romanisation
rom: Resk Merrik, et higil hemm sost, lo et gebb vess sy. Nath re orr o.
english: Merrick, eldest of the ship-masters, sitteth by the door tonight. He is not gone out.

label: Romanisation
rom: Ul et grem hosast tunn re hossvell Yory o um et hald rerddhalden, et hunnat eth nafedh et brodath. Re haever o: Es fimmym pawast lo vorr en scaelur, amm es mymm et cummath dem varn. Gor ryst re vysk Merrik lo: Hess; eth gor ryst re dhyvull Yory: El hosel tevvell o.
english: All that first winter Jory whistled it on the east wall, the tune and never the words. He meant, when the havens came home, to drink again at my grandmother's fire. Every morning Merrick bade him stop, and every morning Jory laughed. "It is only a rhyme."

label: Romanisation
rom: Ul et ryst sa re senn o, re yalom lo o sest, eth re orr et hunnat ul o lern lo dhrenn et haldorrol. Niss re hossvell o, hosen re hyl o et bunth lo et lyss sost hyor. Hy ull re dhald et tevvell ulom, duss hosen bunth bysket ul hyll losk. Re hunnom et pa dhrenn sa nafedh re veller.
english: On the morning he died I was at his side, and the tune went before him along the wall-walk. Slow he whistled it, as he had turned the rope for the least of us. Then the rhyme stood up hard in me, as a mooring-line at the flood. I heard the two lines we never sang.

label: Romanisation
rom: Re vysk Merrik lo: Hess.
english: Merrick told him to stop.

label: Romanisation
rom: Nath re vyskym lo: Hess.
english: I did not tell him to stop.

label: Romanisation
rom: Ul vimm et haldorrol re vellor sceth ul vorr um et tolmath. Re scyndal o somm re rarr o.
english: Below us a fire-ship came in on the stones, burning. It screamed as it came.

label: Romanisation
rom: Re hess et hunnat.
english: The tune stopped.

label: Romanisation
rom: Sol o ul et stell hosast um et lern rerddhalden.
english: His is the first cairn on the east face.

label: Romanisation
rom: Amm ston lest en scaelur tul, haemer et sull tolm ryss myst ul susk odh sennet, eth nath noss crisur lont veth et helvnynth.
english: If my grandmother's house stand yet, the three grey stones hang there over a cold hearth, under no roof but the rain.

label: Romanisation
rom: Nadhumar. Gor fedh re nadhumar gell. Veth tum Mesk Myst.
english: We forget. We have always been good at that. But Mystwood remembers.

label: Romanisation · the laying
rom: Cadhom o hosen re yal cadhat lom.
english: This I lay as it was laid for me.

label: Romanisation · the hearth’s answer
rom: Eth re vysk et odh: Tumar.
english: *And the hearth said: We remember.*

label: Romanisation · the title
rom: Rellor Hosast
english: V.1 · The First Glyph

label: Romanisation · the dateline
rom: Ul et grem hosast, lo rask wress hosast.
english: *The first winter, at the first month's end.*

label: Romanisation · Seren’s headnote
rom: Re hadh Seren Pa Luth, sa re heth et greller. Doss grull et dhysal ull ul lodh et flennath sy tul.
english: *Laid by Seren Two-Inks, that held the lamp. The sand of that shingle is in the binding of this Book yet.*

label: Romanisation
rom: Keth et tolm, Seren.
english: Hold the stone, Seren.

label: Romanisation
rom: Um et dhysal re hethe Halyna et mesk, eth re hethym et greller: gemm garl lonta um et meskdhrenn, eth hos lom. Hosen ull re hadhar et tolm hosast; eth hosen ull ser o tul.
english: On the shingle {{Halyna}} held the wood, and I held the lamp: their four hands on the grain, and my one. As it began, so it hath gone on.

label: Romanisation
rom: Hos bress, ell virr, re solant et wemmeth myst ul lern et hald sy, eth re sesk nahos hyor vodh ew so. Ul et vess sa re yal et kiser hosast cresket, re lymm et hyll et kaelir ul vimm et hald: crynireth myst, crestalath cresket, breller sell hosen ganna. Re scaevur o ul et venth fedh eth fedh, hosen amm re hyl et wadh gor saedel dem veskyl et vimmlern.
english: Nigh a month had the grey sails lain off this wall, and what they were, none of us wist. The night the first assault was broken, the tide brought their wreck in under the wall: grey planks, broken ribs, a keel as long as a gate. Over and over it rolled in the shallows, as though the sea were turning each piece to see its underside.

label: Romanisation
rom: Nath re orrant et farrardath hemm hy et hald. Re orrant et hesperdeth, eth re hadhant vorrath hyo um et hylldhrenn, hy vodh ew merr et mesk um et sorth. Vorra o, re vysk Harl Orrow sa Vorr. Re hresk o hos crestal hyo um o yerd, eth re hebb o dem et vorr. Hos eth hos re dhald et vorrath, hosen taldant grellereth lo dhrenn dhavow ul hedh. Re lusk et Crenn so ul vorrol et saed strom hyo, eth re ston et Crenn ul so lodh, sol.
english: The old sailors on the wall would not go nigh it. The soldiers went, and made their fires of it along the tide-line, for wood was dear on the ridge. "Burn it," said Harl of the burning shore. He broke a rib of it across his knee, and fed it in. One by one the fires went up, as lamps go up along a quay at dusk. The Captain let them burn the most of it, and stood among them, still.

label: Romanisation
rom: Somm re hyn et vorrath hosast, re rarr Hale Haskard dem susk hy et hylldhrenn. Lo sest et vorrath re orr o, eth lo sest et Crenn, dem Halyna.
english: While the first fires caught, Hale the runner came up from the water's edge. Past the fires he went, and past the Captain, to {{Halyna}}.

label: Romanisation
rom: Rellorath um et mesk.
english: "Marks on the wood."

label: Romanisation
rom: Lo hylyl et hyll re orra Halyna dem vimm, garl Halvard ul vimm sestyarl Hyna um et tolmath thenth. Re rarrom ul sestow, eth et greller lom; hy vodh ew sullast Halyna en, eth re yal lymmyl et baegyth lom. Re wammant et uldath hos crynir dem susk hy et spant, eth re hadhom et greller lo.
english: At the turn of the tide {{Halyna}} went down, Halvard's hand under Rhyna's elbow on the wet stones. I came behind with the lamp, for I was their third, and the light was mine to carry. The men hauled one plank up out of the surf, and I set the lamp down by it.

label: Romanisation
rom: Lo dhrenn o veskdhrenn re orr hos rellor, bynt eth venthen hosen stinel hosast dholmard. Ew clenn hos cless sell, treskat lo dhrenn et meskdhrenn, hosen amm re yal et ullen treskat hyo.
english: Along its grain ran one figure, fine and shallow as a mason's first scoring. One long edge was raw, split down the grain, as if the rest had been torn away.

label: Romanisation
rom: Hy yalatath sa ross brodhol lont, re yal lor et tolmath nawrodh ul vestul rytow, eth havul ul vimm hosk Wendhessa, sa nath re nahosk hos ganna. Amm sy re yal et crynir lor. Re rytent gostardath et gostol lo so nunthath: Hebb et mesk domm kaever ul narl uld, amm sol o yarl umo loskat. Re dhyvull et Orrow umont. Re yal nayalat ullen lor dem raevulol.
english: Of things that might speak, we had the mute stones in the archive chest, and a bundle under the seal of {{Wendhessa}} that no pair would break. Now we had this. Axemen of the felling had sworn in their cups that the black wood would put a thought into a man's hand, if he rested it there long enough. The shore had laughed at them. Naught else was left us to try.

label: Romanisation
rom: Hy ull re resk Rhyna lo et crynir, eth re hadh ey pa yarlremull ryss um et meskdhrenn. Re lumm Halvard ul sestow, eth re hadh o pa yarl umont. Nath re wrodha. Re rarr et hyll, eth re orr. Re vorr et greller dem vimm ryssyth nind.
english: So Rhyna sat down by the plank, and laid her palms flat on the grain. Halvard kneeled behind her, and laid his hands over hers. They spake not. The tide came and went. The lamp burned down a finger's width.

label: Romanisation
rom: Hy ull re dhald et kethyl ul narlremullath Hyna. Re vorr o, re vysk ey, nel hosen vorr, veth hosen dusstyvil brid ul molt et grem. Ul et vorrol re yal et lern: hos stinel ul gylyl dem lern, hosen fodh sa es gresk. Nath re wrodh ey tul, eth re wemm Halvard o wisk.
english: Then the knowing came up into Rhyna's palms. It burned, she said, not as fire, but as cold iron in the deep of winter. Its shape was in the burning: one stroke curling forward, like a wave about to break. With no word from her, Halvard lifted his head.

label: Romanisation
rom: Orrow, re vysk o.
english: "Shore," he said.

label: Romanisation
rom: Re vysk Rhyna: El venn o.
english: Rhyna said that he was right.

label: Romanisation
rom: Nath re yal myskyl lo Halvard hosen vodh re heth o o. Ew hosen amm re hadh hos et brod ul o wrodow, re vysk o, eth re orr dem neld. Re hethe mest hy et brod; veth ew kaever lurr et ullen, eth nath re yal veth kaever et orrow lonta. Re hethe o somm re vorr et greller dem vimm, eth nath re yal brodhol lonta veth hos brod.
english: How he knew it, Halvard could not say. It was as though one had put the word into his mouth, he said, and gone away. More than the word they knew, but the rest was a forest's thought, and they had but the shore's. Till the lamp was low they held it, and one word was all they could tell.

label: Romanisation
rom: Re dhalda niss hy et tolmath, eth re rarrant ullen dem vimm dem raevulol. Hosast re rarr Yory Dhavow Hemm, sa resk vess sy ul sestow et hellur sy, lo sest Voss. Re hadh o yarl umo, ul dhyvullol. Crynireth thenth, re vysk o, eth re orr o dem susk et dhysal ul hossvellyl, et hunnat eth nafedh et brodath.
english: They rose stiff from the stones, and others came down to try it. First came Jory of Eldhythe, that sitteth tonight at the back of this hall, beside Voss. He laid his hand on it, laughing. "Wet planks," said he, and went up the shingle whistling, the tune and never the words.

label: Romanisation
rom: Hy ull re rarra Enno eth Della, sa re orra dem susk et brunn garl ul narl. Re hadha gemm garl um et crynir olen. Re vysk o: El brid et mesk; eth re vysk ey: Nel; eth ew venn pana.
english: Then came Enno and Della, that walked up the mountain hand in hand. Their four hands they laid on the plank together. He said the wood was cold, and she said it was not, and both were right.

label: Romanisation
rom: Amm re orra, re reskym ul vodh re resk Rhyna. Hosel re hadhom en narlremull sost um et meskdhrenn. Re dhald galat ulo hy et mesk, strom hy hethyl. Ew rhull losk o, eth nemm en, eth nunth lom.
english: When they had gone, I sat where Rhyna had sat. Alone I laid mine own palm on the grain. Something came up into it out of the wood, too great to hold. It was a river in flood, and I a girl with a cup.

label: Romanisation
rom: Re luskom.
english: I let go.

label: Romanisation
rom: Fedh pawast re hadh Halvard et greller ul en narl.
english: Halvard put the lamp back in mine hand.

label: Romanisation
rom: Nath re orrar dem susk tul; re lunnom et flennath sy um et gerdeth, lo flenn midh, veth ew merr et flenneth amm ull. Ul molt et flenn re hadhom hos brod, orrow, eth nayalat ullen. Nath re femm et luth o tul, eth re vyskym o sull fedh, hosen myskym gor wrod, dem hunnol ho heth o. Re heth o. Ew nasell o, eth gemmyorn; eth re resk o ul et brodow hosen tolm ul et lodh.
english: Before we went up, I opened this Book on my knees at a clean leaf, though leaves were dear then. In the middle I set one word, *shore*, and naught else. Ere the ink touched it, I said it over three times, as I do with every word, to hear whether it would hold. It held. Short it was, and square, and it sat in the mouth as a dressed stone in its bed.

label: Romanisation
rom: Um et flenn ul lern re rytym et rellor. Ul helv et wadh nath re wroc et luth.
english: On the facing leaf I drew the sign. In the sea air the ink would not dry.

label: Romanisation
rom: Ew lyss sost et brod um o flenn.
english: The word looked very small on its leaf.

label: Romanisation
rom: Re rarrar dem susk, eth et vorrath vimm ul sestow. Lo et ganna re hesse Halyna.
english: We came up with the fires low behind us. At the gate {{Halyna}} stopped.

label: Romanisation
rom: Re rarr uld myst et trenn hemm dem nebb, eth re yal sull brod lo, eth nath re yal trenn wrodath.
english: "The grey man of the old tale came to a door with three words, and no sentence."

label: Romanisation
rom: Eth doss hos brod lona.
english: "And we have one word."

label: Romanisation · the laying
rom: Cadhom o hosen re yal cadhat lom.
english: This I lay as it was laid for me.

label: Romanisation · the hearth’s answer
rom: Eth re vysk et odh: Tumar.
